key_insight: MANTRA tests whether early angiotensin-II, compared with norepinephrine, can better correct RAAS dysfunction and reshape immune responses in septic shock.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this strategy could identify a biomarker-guided vasopressor approach for a high-risk shock population rather than relying on norepinephrine alone.
method: Multicenter, open-label, randomized 1:1 trial in adults with septic shock on norepinephrine-equivalent 0.10–0.50 mcg/kg/min
Primary arm: angiotensin-II up to 40 ng/kg/min vs norepinephrine up to 35 mcg/min for 48 hours
Primary endpoint: change in plasma renin from baseline to 24 hours using a linear mixed-effects model
evidence_signal: This is a study protocol, not results; the abstract reports planned enrollment of 78 patients and 90% power to detect a 25% between-group difference in 24-hour renin.
watch_item: Open-label design and mechanistic focus mean clinical benefit, safety, and generalizability may remain uncertain until outcomes are reported.
paper_title: Mechanistic Assessment of Norepinephrine Therapy versus Angiotensin-II in Septic Shock (MANTRA): Study Protocol for a multicenter randomized trial
